sentences: RDNA2 keeps f16 denormals, so every module also declares `OpExecutionMode %main DenormPreserve 16` (capability `DenormPreserve`, core since SPIR-V 1.4 like `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, so no extension at `--target-env vulkan1.2`).

The translator models f16 arithmetic in f32 with integer narrowing (`Gen.f16_bits`), so an f16 denormal is an ordinary f32 value in the module and no f32 denormal is involved: the 16-bit mode is what governs the f16→f32 conversion the driver emits for an f16 source.

NVIDIA flushed that conversion without it: in `runtime/test/shaders/ps_sdwa_f16_const.asm` the y lane (`src0_sel:BYTE_1` of `2.0` is the denormal 0x0040 = 2^−18, × 1024.0 = 2^−8 = 0x1c00) read 0x0000, 4096/4096 pixels wrong, while x, z and w matched; with the mode the test is 4096/4096 exact (RTX 4070 SUPER, driver 610.88, Windows 11, validation layers on).
The same lane read 0x0000 on an RTX 3090 (driver 610.88, found by @Rainmaker33).
Assembling the same module with only the two `DenormPreserve` lines removed reads 0x0000 again, so it is the mode the driver honours, not a change in the translated code.
Not every NVIDIA build flushes it: on `main` without the mode an RTX 4060 Ti (621.24), an RTX 5070 Ti (620.73.04, Linux) and an RTX 5080 (616.92) pass the test.

The index entry lists `"shaderDenormPreserveFloat16"` after `"shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32"`; `vk_pipeline_check` skips the shader where the device reports that property false, and `--no-float-controls` leaves both modes out.

Where the property is false the module has no f16 denormal guarantee, so an f16 denormal read can come back +0 exactly as in that lane above (NVIDIA's default without the mode); that is a value difference in the shader, and the GPU test's y lane is then expected to fail.

The AMD Radeon iGPU (RDNA2, driver 24.10.24, Vulkan 1.3.280) reports `shaderDenormPreserveFloat16` true with `denormBehaviorIndependence` `32_BIT_ONLY`, and `vk_pipeline_check` builds the module and its pipeline there (`ps_sdwa_f16_const`: 1 module ok, 1 pipeline ok, wave32 and wave64); the GPU test itself skips on that device, which has 128 push-constant bytes where the test needs 144.
`tests/semantic/test_f16_denorm_preserve.py` pins the mode, the index property and the four words.
